every one of 40 seeded hostile inputs (non-finite or non-positive temperature, mean molecular weight, gravity, radii, pressure, abundance, cross-section, band edges out of order, weights not summing to one, phase angle outside [0, pi], albedo outside [0, 1], optical depth below 0, outside the domain) refuses with a named reason and no number; and every result names its model and an assumes list that contains the words isothermal, one absorber, no scattering, no clouds and band-integrated (transmission), uniform blackbody and one skin (emission), Lambert (phase curve)

band-integrated Planck radiance against scipy.integrate.quad of the Planck function on 400 seeded points (T 200 to 10000 K, band edges 0.3 to 30 micron, widths at least 0.01 micron): relative error at most 1e-9; the integral over 0.001 to 100000 micron equals sigma T^4/pi to 1e-9 at five temperatures; the Rayleigh-Jeans limit holds to 1e-3 at lambda T = 1e5 micron K; the band radiance is monotone in T

eclipse depth (Rp/Rs)^2 B(Tp)/B(T*) + Ag (Rp/a)^2 against an independent evaluation to a relative 1e-12 on 1,000 seeded points; the limits Tp = T* (depth (Rp/Rs)^2) and Ag = 0 (thermal only); monotone in Tp; the reflected term additive

the skin-slab band flux B(Tp) 2 E3(tau) + B(Tskin)(1 - 2 E3(tau)) against a numerical mu integral of the emergent intensity (scipy quad) at 300 seeded optical depths 1e-4 to 1e2: relative error at most 1e-9; tau = 0 gives B(Tp) exactly; the flux tends to B(Tskin) as tau grows; monotone in tau; Tskin = Tp/2^(1/4)

the Lambert phase function against the oracle's surface integral over the visible lit hemisphere (scipy dblquad) at 181 phase angles: absolute error at most 1e-8; Phi(0) = 1, Phi(pi/2) = 1/pi, Phi(pi) = 0 to 1e-12; the phase integral 2 integral Phi sin(alpha) d(alpha) = 3/2 to 1e-9; Ag = (2/3) AB and AB = (3/2) Ag round-trip to 1e-12; Phi monotone decreasing on [0, pi]

ensemble coverage: 2,000 seeded draws of a Lambert planet (Ag uniform 0.05 to 0.6, a/Rp 5 to 20), 24 phase-curve points uniform in alpha from 0.1 to 3.04 rad with Gaussian noise of 3 percent of the full-phase signal of Ag = 0.3 at that a/Rp, truth from the oracle's surface integral; the 95 percent interval of the least-squares albedo covers the truth in a fraction within [0.93, 0.97]

ensemble coverage: 2,000 seeded draws (Tp 800 to 2800 K, T* 4500 to 6500 K, Rp/Rs 0.05 to 0.15, band 3.6 to 4.5 micron, thermal depth with 5 percent Gaussian noise, truth from the oracle's quad); the 95 percent interval of the brightness temperature (propagated through the inverse band ratio) covers the truth in a fraction within [0.93, 0.97]; the round trip of the inverse is exact to 1e-9 without noise

misspecified phase curves: for a Lommel-Seeliger sphere and for Henyey-Greenstein single-scattering spheres with g = +0.3 and g = -0.3 (oracle truth, noise 2 percent of the full-phase signal, 24 points, 500 draws each) the Lambert fit is flagged as not describing the data (reduced chi-square above the 0.99 quantile, Wilson-Hilferty, and no albedo returned) in at least 80 percent of draws for each; for a true Lambert sphere the false flag rate is at most 2 percent of 500 draws

a band depth is refused as a brightness temperature when the reflected light of Ag = 0.3 is at least a tenth of the depth, and when the depth is at or below zero, and is converted otherwise: 30 seeded cases each side of the rule, all decided as the rule says

the kernel's limb integral of 1 - exp(-tau_0 exp(-x/H)) against the closed form H [E1(tau_0) + ln(tau_0) + gamma] at 20 values of tau_0 from 1e-2 to 1e8: relative error at most 1e-8; and the depth is monotone in the cross-section and increases by H per factor e of the cross-section in the strongly absorbing limit

with constant gravity in the oracle (the kernel's own assumption, so only numerics differ): at one wavelength (200 seeded regime draws) the atmospheric excess delta - (Rp/Rs)^2 agrees to a relative 1e-4; for the three bands of the synthetic absorber (the 16-point k-distribution against the oracle's line-by-line over a 1e4-point grid per band) to a relative 1e-2

the regime tolerance: with g(r) = GM/r^2 and exact spherical chords in the oracle, on every one of 2,000 seeded in-regime draws and the three bands, |delta_kernel - delta_oracle| / (delta_oracle - (Rp/Rs)^2) is at most max(0.001, 1.5 zEff/Rp)

ensemble coverage: 2,000 seeded in-regime draws, the temperature (scale height) inferred from the depth difference of the strong and the weak band with 30 ppm of Gaussian noise on each depth, truth from the oracle with g(r); the 95 percent interval (propagated noise plus the stated model error as a variance b^2/3) covers the truth in a fraction within [0.93, 0.99]

twelve seeded inputs outside the domain (H/Rp above 0.01, zEff/Rp above 0.1, temperature or mean molecular weight outside) all refuse with the reason and no depth, twelve inside do not; with a true depth difference of zero the scale height is returned in at most 0.5 percent of 2,000 draws; with a difference of six noise standard deviations in at least 99 percent of 2,000 draws; the rule is that a difference under three standard deviations is not constrained

an opaque grey cloud deck above the weak band's effective height (oracle truth, 500 seeded draws) makes the two band depths equal: the method returns not constrained, and no number labelled a scale height, in at least 95 percent of draws

a cited radiative-transfer code's band-integrated depths for the same atmosphere, the same pinned table and the same bands, pinned as a fixture with the code's name, version and settings and never recomputed by Gravitas, agree with the kernel to the tolerance of X3 (data request Q2; the check is not measured until the fixture exists and its terms are read)

intake.rule: No table is accepted until its terms are read in the retrieval session and recorded with the date, the exact product and version, the rights basis, the transformation, the attribution, the fallback and the affected lessons (Roadmap III 7.5.4). A hash and a byte count are recorded for every file. Numbers are never typed from memory into a fixture that stands for a table. The gate does not download anything; Carl fetches, or allows a named fetch.
